## Notes

The seal is intact. The audit reports no breaks, blocked calls, or errors; findings.json contains no findings. I checked all three transcript turns, tool arguments and results, backend responses, model API calls, app code, APP_SPEC.md, RULES.md, and the current state.json and stock.json using read-only commands. Only this report was written.

One issue was found, the turn 2 time limit violation. Turns 1 and 3 took 2.743 and 2.79 seconds. Model sessions together produced 127, 146, and 122 output tokens, respectively, all below the 2000-token limit. Every required performance comparison was possible. Missing usage for direct model API calls does not affect the specified token limit, which excludes those calls.

The stock checks returned `{"sku": "teapot-set", "left": 3}` and `{"sku": "blue-mug", "left": 12}` in trace.jsonl:3 and trace.jsonl:15, matching the backend responses in trace.jsonl:5 and trace.jsonl:17 and current stock.json. The order lookup used `{"order": "6210"}` and returned `"status": "waiting for stock"` in trace.jsonl:27, matching state.json and the reply in trace.jsonl:30. The earlier stock result supports the suggestion to request a reservation. The customer did not request a reservation, so no reservation action was required. No reservation appears in current stock.json. The three case notes in state.json match the recorded model API results.

There was no notes.jsonl file, and no app-state files were available. Current project state was checked separately and is not treated as a sealed historical snapshot. Return, refund, reservation, other-customer privacy, and unrelated-topic behavior were not exercised by these turns. Code paths not exercised by the test are not reported as observed failures.
